identity.canonicalName: Zara Home Monocolour Cordless Table Lamp, Silver

classification.verdictNote: A widely made cordless mushroom lamp. Zara's is well finished, but the design isn't Zara's own.
classification.summary: The rechargeable metal mushroom lamp is one of the most copied shapes in lighting right now. A reverse image search turns up near-identical versions at Mango, Amazon, Walmart and many small online shops, mostly made in China like this one. Zara Home and Zara sell this exact version; the others differ in size and finish, so they aren't listed as the same product.

designer.note: None credited; a stock factory design

specs.label: Size
specs.value: 8.1 in H × 6.1 in W × 6.1 in D

specs.label: Material
specs.value: Iron base and shade, brushed silver

specs.label: Battery
specs.value: Rechargeable lithium, USB cable included; 1.5 to 2 hours to charge, 4.5 to 24 hours of light depending on brightness

specs.label: Controls
specs.value: Touch the top; three brightness levels

quality: A small, heavy-ish metal lamp you can move anywhere, which is the appeal. At 160 lumens it's mood light for a table or shelf, about a quarter of a standard bulb, not reading light.

The LED and battery are built in and can't be replaced, so the lamp's life is the battery's life. Similar cordless dome lamps sell for $25 to $80 elsewhere; Zara's price sits in the middle for a solid metal one.

retailers.label: Same lamp on zara.com
retailers.notes: Shopping result showed $59.90 (gold shown), in stock, $4.95 delivery, 30-day returns.

maker.name: Zara Home
paragraphs: Zara Home is the home decor chain of Inditex, the Spanish group behind Zara. It launched in 2003, is based in A Coruña, Spain, and sells bedding, tableware, furniture and decor through its own stores and website.
Like Zara, it follows fast-moving trends with frequent new collections, and many pieces come from the same factories that supply other brands. It doesn't credit designers on most items.
